sections.title: What a starter is
sections.body:
A sourdough starter is a culture of wild yeast and lactic acid bacteria living in a paste of flour and water.

The yeast produces the gas that raises the bread, and the bacteria produce the acids that give it a sour taste.

> KEY NUMBER: A healthy starter doubles in volume between four and eight hours after it is fed at room temperature.

A starter that does not double within twelve hours is called sluggish and needs two days of regular feeding before it is used.

quiz.q: What produces the gas that raises the bread?
quiz.e: The yeast produces the gas; the bacteria produce the acids.

quiz.q: Within what window does a healthy starter double after a room temperature feed?
quiz.e: Four to eight hours at room temperature.

quiz.q: A starter has not doubled after twelve hours. What does the handout call it and require?
o: Sluggish; two days of regular feeding before use
quiz.e: Sluggish, and it needs two days of regular feeding before it is used.
quiz.src: called sluggish and needs two days of regular feeding

quiz.q: At what temperature does the yeast go dormant?
quiz.e: Invented; the handout never says this.

sections.title: Feeding
sections.lede: Ratios by weight, and a clock.
sections.body:
Feeding means discarding most of the starter and mixing the rest with fresh flour and water.

| Feed | Ratio (starter : flour : water, by weight) | Use |
|---|---|---|
| Standard | 1:1:1 | The standard feed |
| Stiff | 1:2:1 | Slows fermentation; when the starter will sit for more than a day |

The standard feed is one part starter, one part flour, and one part water by weight, written as 1:1:1. A stiff feed of 1:2:1 slows fermentation and is used when the starter will sit for more than a day.

> TRAP: Always use water below 30 degrees Celsius, because hotter water kills the yeast.

- Feed a starter kept at room temperature once every twenty four hours.

quiz.q: What is the standard feed ratio?

o: When the starter will sit for more than a day
quiz.e: A stiff feed slows fermentation for a longer wait.

quiz.q: Why must the water be below 30 degrees Celsius?
quiz.e: The handout gives one reason: hotter water kills the yeast.

quiz.q: How often is a refrigerated starter fed?

sections.title: Reading the signs
sections.body:
| Sign | Meaning | Action |
|---|---|---|
| Gray liquid on top (hooch) | Hungry | Feed sooner |
| Pink or orange streaks | Contaminated | Throw the whole starter away |
| Nail polish remover smell | Overdue for a feed | Still safe to use |
| Floats in water | Ready | Bake with it |

A layer of gray liquid on top, called hooch, means the starter is hungry and should be fed sooner. Pink or orange streaks mean the culture is contaminated and the whole starter must be thrown away. A smell of nail polish remover means the starter is overdue for a feed but is still safe to use. The float test drops a spoonful of starter into water; if it floats, the starter is ready to bake with.

o: The starter is hungry and should be fed sooner
The starter is ready to bake with
quiz.e: Gray liquid on top means hungry.

quiz.q: Which sign means the whole starter must be thrown away?
quiz.e: Contamination; the other signs are recoverable.

quiz.q: The starter smells of nail polish remover. Which is true?
o: It is overdue for a feed but still safe to use
It is ready to bake with
It needs two days of regular feeding
quiz.src: overdue for a feed but is still safe to use

quiz.q: A starter will wait two days before baking. Which feed fits?
quiz.e: Stiff feed for more than a day.
